dish: Big stacked burgers on griddled hard buns (Sparky Burger) and the 'Captain Kangaroo taco rice'
n: Captain Kangaroo, Nago (キャプテンカンガルー)
w: A burger shop that began as an Osaka bar in 1999 and opened in Nago in 2007, moving to its current Umusa site in 2020. Stars and Stripes Okinawa calls it a hot spot for its taco rice as well as its burgers; OTV Okitive profiles its Mexican-loaded 'Captain Kangaroo taco rice', and Smart Magazine ranks it among Okinawa's top one or two burger shops.

dish: Burgers with an Okinawa-raised pork patty
address: Nago Jūjiro arcade (名護十字路), Nago-shi, Okinawa, Japan
w: A burger shop opened in June 2022 in a renovated unit of the old Nago Jūjiro arcade in central Nago. OTV Okitive singles out its patty made mainly from Okinawa-raised pork; Ryukyu Shimpo covered the opening and Stars and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it.

dish: Yanbaru-sugi (farmed cobia) set meals — sugi carpaccio and sugi fry
n: Kaneyan Shokudō, Higashi (かねやん食堂)
w: A mountain-side diner in Higashi village that Okinawa CLIP calls a hidden gem for 'Yanbaru-sugi', the farmed cobia raised in Okinawa's warm sea, served in hearty set meals. Ryukyu Shimpo reported on the diner handing out 100-yen bentos to residents after the Yanbaru heavy-rain disaster.

dish: Kaisen-don of that day's catch and ika-sumi-jiru (squid-ink soup)
n: Nago Fishing Port Fish Market & Diner (名護漁港水産物直販所)
w: A fish-sales hall with an attached diner inside Nago fishing port on Route 58, cooking fish auctioned that day at the port. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā aji māi' column praised its seafood bowl of many fish, Okinawa Times' driver-lunch column went for the squid-ink soup and tempura, and the Nago tourism association lists it.

dish: Shīkwāsā juice tasting by harvest month, and dishes made with shīkwāsā powder
n: Ōgimi Shīkwāsā Park (大宜味シークヮーサーパーク)
w: Billed by the OCVB as Okinawa's first shīkwāsā theme park, in the citrus's home village of Ōgimi: a free-entry factory where you watch the pressing line, compare juices from each month's harvest and eat in a restaurant cooking with shīkwāsā powder. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its completion as a local-produce revitalisation project; the Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists it.

dish: Cheese-and-vegetable taco rice (beef, Koshihikari rice) and 15 cm jumbo cheeseburger
w: A retro-American diner facing Camp Hansen's Gate 1 in Kin, the birthplace of taco rice; Kin town's tourism site lists its big cheese-and-vegetable taco rice, jumbo burger and fried chicken, and notes it takes US dollars as well as yen. Stars and Stripes Okinawa names Gate 1, with King Tacos, as a long-running taco-rice favourite in Kin.

dish: New York cheesecake and house-roasted coffee
n: Bookcafe Okinawa Rail, Kunigami (ブックカフェ オキナワレイル)
address: 2040-107 Ōho-shagahara, Okuma, Kunigami-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
w: An off-grid concrete book café on the forest road toward Yonaha-dake inside Yanbaru National Park, named for the Yanbaru kuina (Okinawa rail), running on solar power and spring water with walls of books. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its opening as a forest reading retreat; OTV Okitive calls it worth the trip, and Tabirai recommends the New York cheesecake and house-roasted coffee.
